subject: SLA harmonization: regional uptime baseline, latency carve-outs, and monthly credit tiers
messages:
From: Claire Park <cpark@stellarnet.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-legal@stellarnet.com, procurement@stellarnet.com
Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 16:11:00 +0100
Subject: Draft SLA: baseline uptime and credits (first pass)

Hi Logan,

Thanks for sending over the initial SLA template. We're reviewing the uptime ladder and the monthly credit mechanics. A few quick items from our side:

- StellarNet typically needs a 99.95% commitment for core API endpoints in EU prod. Can you confirm Redwood's standard baseline and if you can commit to that for our regional pool?
- We need clarity on how credits are calculated for degraded throughput vs full outage (is it a token-based reconciliation or flat monthly cap?).
- Any exceptions for scheduled maintenance windows and batch processing spikes? Our legal team asks for explicit carve-outs.

I've attached our procurement checklist and highlighted sections where we expect tighter language.

Best,
Claire
Head of Platform Ops, StellarNet

Attachments: StellarNet_SLA_Redwood_Template_v1.2.pdf, procurement-checklist.docx

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <cpark@stellarnet.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 23 Jun 2025 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft SLA: baseline uptime and credits (first pass)

Claire — thanks for the notes and the attachment. Quick answers up front:

- Redwood standard hosted baseline is 99.9% for free-tier customers; for committed/Dedicated we typically offer 99.95% as the standard enterprise baseline. We can propose 99.95% for your EU regional pool subject to capacity reservation (outlined below).
- Credits: our usual approach is a monthly service-credit ladder calculated as a percentage of the monthly invoice for the affected service (we can also provide token-based reconciliation if you prefer more granular accounting). The draft you received shows the ladder; I'll attach an example calculation (uptime-calculation-example.xlsx).
- Exceptions: scheduled maintenance windows are excluded if notified with 72 hours lead time; we also have a limited carve-out for batched inference where latency SLOs don't apply during warm-up/burst periods.

Let's pull legal on a short call to walk through carve-outs and to confirm the reserve capacity terms that back the 99.95% commitment. Suggested times below.

—Logan
Director, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Attachments: uptime-calculation-example.xlsx

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <cpark@stellarnet.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 10:28:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Draft SLA: baseline uptime and credits (regarding maintenance and latency carve-outs)

Claire / Logan,

Following up from our side with more detail on the maintenance and latency carve-outs to reduce back-and-forth:

- Maintenance: we propose a monthly maintenance budget of up to 6 hours per region as non-creditable, with a rolling 12-month cap (i.e., scheduled maintenance beyond the monthly budget should be mutually agreed). We will notify 72h in advance for planned major upgrades.

- Latency SLOs: For the hosted API we propose p95 latency targets of 150ms for single-request interactive traffic and a separate p95 500ms target for queued/batched jobs. We will exclude the batched job window (up to 10 minutes per scheduled batch) from latency SLA calculations.

- Credits calculation: we can offer two modes — percentage-of-invoice ladder (standard) or token-based reconciliation. For StellarNet's use case (mixed interactive and batch workloads), token-based makes sense — we can map tokens to weighted buckets and show sample math in the workbook.

If this direction works, we can put these bullets into redline-friendly language for your counsel.

Laura Bennett
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference

From: ops-legal@stellarnet.com <ops-legal@stellarnet.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Park <cpark@stellarnet.com>, procurement@stellarnet.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 11:51:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Draft SLA: baseline uptime and credits (legal quick comments)

Laura / Logan —

Thanks for the details. A couple of legal points from StellarNet:

1) The 6-hour monthly maintenance carve-out is acceptable if it is region-specific and non-aggregating across regions — please reflect that.
2) We need tighter language around "notify 72h in advance" — request a minimum of 5 business days for any maintenance that could affect production traffic, except for emergency fixes.
3) Credits: StellarNet prefers a monthly cap equal to 100% of the affected service's monthly spend rather than an absolute cap across the entire account. Can Redwood provide an example cap calculation?

We'd like to run a single redline against your template rather than iterate prose — Claire, can we schedule legal + ops + Redwood legal on Thursday?

— Ops Legal (StellarNet)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Claire Park <cpark@stellarnet.com>, ops-legal@stellarnet.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft SLA: baseline uptime and credits (confirming redline call)

Claire / Ops Legal — thanks for the comments. Thursday 2025-06-26 at 14:00 UTC works for Redwood legal + commercial to join a redline session. Agenda: 1) confirm regional maintenance notice window, 2) agree on monthly cap mechanics (we'll show example math from the workbook), 3) finalize latency carve-out wording for batched inference.

I'll upload a short one-pager summarizing the proposed credit calculations to the Drive link shared previously ahead of the call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Manager, Account Strategy — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: StellarNet_SLA_Redwood_Template_v1.2.pdf, uptime-calculation-example.xlsx
